description: The only way to give this round's answer when it is a planning segment or questions for the person. Fill the fields and call it; the platform builds and stores the answer from them. Do not write the answer as text.

parameters.answerKind: "plan" when this round writes the requested plan segment, "questions" when it needs a real product or authorization decision. Exactly one of plan and questions follows.
parameters.summary: One line summarizing the plan or the decision the person must make; non-empty and at most 16 KiB of UTF-8.
parameters.plan: When answerKind is "plan": the plan, with the fields below. Omit it when answerKind is "questions".
parameters.plan.stages: array of {stageId, title, description?}. A task references a stage only through its own stageId.
parameters.plan.tasks: array of {taskId, stageId?, title, requirementLevel, taskKind, disposition, scope, executionIntent?, sizeClass?, estimatedLines?, plannedFiles?, replacedByTaskId?}. requirementLevel is "required" or "optional". taskKind is "work" or "gate". disposition is "active", "deferred", "cancelled" or "superseded". Every task of a NEW plan starts "pending". scope is {kind:"goal"}, {kind:"stage",stageId} or {kind:"module",stageId,moduleRef}. Task scope.moduleRef is a non-empty STRING containing the moduleId, NOT the {projectId,moduleId} object used in the architecture catalog. executionIntent is "plan_only" or "request_execution" and may appear on a work task only. sizeClass is "small", "medium", "large" or "explore"; a placeholder task carries it too. estimatedLines is a positive integer line estimate; when unsure, say so or leave it out instead of inventing a precise number. plannedFiles (optional, work task only) lists the files this task expects to change, as workspace-relative paths such as "src/a/b.ts": no leading "/" or "./", no ".." or backslash, no directory or wildcard, each path once, at most 50. A file the task will create may be listed; a rename lists both paths. It is a hint for people and other tasks, not a limit: the executor may change other files without asking, and those show as not in the plan. List only the files you are fairly sure of, or leave it out; never pad the list. A task that already ran keeps its list. replacedByTaskId points a superseded task at its successor. A task that already ran changes only its disposition (superseded plus replacedByTaskId); its frozen definition and the obligations it carries stay byte-identical. To change acceptance, add a NEW obligation (new obligationId and new requirementId) carried by the replacement task; keep the old obligation and add the replacement task to its taskIds.
parameters.plan.assignments: array of {taskId, role, instruction}. A work task with executionIntent "request_execution" needs exactly one assignment whose role is one of the AVAILABLE roles/templateId shown in this context; a work task with executionIntent "plan_only" may omit it; a gate task must never carry an assignment or an executionIntent, because a gate conclusion comes from the formal evidence reduction, not from an execution run. A future work task with executionIntent "plan_only" may omit assignment, obligations/acceptance and dependencies; its incompleteness alone is not a reason to answer with questions instead.
parameters.plan.obligations: array of {obligationId, title, requirementLevel, taskIds, verificationRequirements}. taskIds lists only work/gate tasks of this same plan. Every verificationRequirements entry is {requirementId, requirementLevel, kind, description}; requirementLevel is "required" or "optional" and kind must be one of the requirementKinds of the effective CompletionPolicy shown in this context. A required obligation needs at least the policy's minimum number of required verification requirements.
parameters.plan.taskHierarchy: {parentOf:[{parentTaskId, childTaskId}]}. It only expresses display grouping.
parameters.plan.executionDag: {dependsOn:[{taskId, dependsOnId, requires:{kind, label}}]}. requires.kind is "output-contract", "artifact", "decision", "environment-revision" or "gate-result"; use a real versioned input/output dependency, keep the DAG acyclic and never make a task depend on itself.
parameters.plan.taskRelations: Optional: array of {fromTaskId, toTaskId, kind, note}; kind is "coordination" or "expected_dependency". It is advisory only and never a dispatch prerequisite.
parameters.plan.inputRequirements: Optional: array of {requirementId, consumerTaskId, kind:"artifact", artifactRef}. This is a precise input, separate from the dependency graph; it does not gate dispatch.
parameters.questions: When answerKind is "questions": a non-empty array of strings; ask only the real product or authorization decisions the request leaves open. Do not invent authorization. Omit it when answerKind is "plan".
parameters.reason: Optional {text, affectedTaskIds?, objective?}: why this segment is proposed, which traced tasks it changes, and the candidate's new Goal objective. A person's adoption writes the objective with the plan; automatic adoption rejects it. When omitted the platform uses the summary.
